groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Hi, my name's Cathy. Nice to meet you!
M: Nice to meet you too, Cathy. My name's John. I'm a university friend of the bride. What about you? Who do you know at this party?
W: I am a colleague of Brenda. I was a little surprised to be invited, to be honest. We've only been working together the last six months, but we quickly became good friends. We just wrapped up a project with a difficult client last week. I bet Brenda is glad it's done with, and she can focus on wedding preparations.
M: Oh, yes, so you're Cathy from the office. Actually I've heard a lot about you, and that project. The client sounded like a real nightmare.
W: Oh, he was. I mean we deal with all kinds of people on a regular basis. It's part of the job, but he was especially particular, enough about that. What line of work are you in?
M: Well, right out of college, I worked in advertising for a while. Recently though, I turned my photography hobby into a small business. I'll actually be taking photos during the big event as a wedding gift.
W: That sounds wonderful, and very thoughtful of you. I bake just as a hobby but Brenda has asked me to do the cake for the wedding. I was a bit nervous saying yes, because I'm far from a professional.
M: Did you bake the cookies here at the party tonight?
W: Yes, I got the idea from a magazine.
M: They're delicious. You've got nothing to worry about. You're a natural.
W: You really think so?
M: If you hadn't told me that, I would have guessed they were baked by the restaurant. You know, with your event planning experience, you could very well open your own shop.
W: One step at a time. First I'll see how baking the wedding cake goes. If it's not a disaster, maybe I'll give it some more thought.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: You are heading for a completely different world now that you are about to graduate from high school.
W: I know it's the end of high school, but many of my classmates are going on to the same university and we are still required to study hard, so what's the difference?
M: Many aspects are different here at university. The most important one is that you have to take more individual responsibility for your actions. It's up to your own self-discipline how much effort you put into study. Living in college dormitories, there are no parents to tell you to study harder or stop wasting time. Lecturers have hundreds of students and they are not going to follow you up or question you if you miss their lectures.
W: Nobody cares, you mean?
M: It's not that nobody is concerned about you. It's just that suddenly at university you are expected to behave like an adult, that means concentrating on the direction of your life in general and your own academic performance specifically.
W: For example?
M: Well, like you need to manage your daily, weekly and monthly schedules so that you will study regularly. Be sure to attend all classes and leave enough time to finish assignments and prepare well for examinations.
W: Okay, and what else is different?
M: Well, in college there are lots of distractions and you need to control yourself. You will make interesting friends, but you need only keep the friends who respect your student commitments. Also, there are a lot of wonderful clubs, but you shouldn't allocate too much time to club activities, unless they are directly related to your study. It's also your choice if you want to go out at night, but you will be foolish to let that affect your class performance during the day.
W: Well, I'm determined to do well at university and I guess I am going to have to grow up fast.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Most successful people are unorthodox persons whose minds wander outside traditional ways of thinking. Instead of trying to refine old formulas, they invent new ones.
When Jean-Claude Killy made the French national ski team in the early 1960s, he was prepared to work harder than anyone else to be the best. At the crack of dawn he would run up the slopes with his skis on, an unbelievably backbreaking activity. In the evening he would do weight lifting and running. But the other team members were working as hard and long as he was. He realized instinctively that simply training harder would never be enough.
Killy then began challenging the basic theories of racing technique. Each week he would try something different to see if he could find a better, faster way down the mountain. His experiments resulted in a new style that was almost exactly opposite the accepted technique of the time. It involved skiing with his legs apart for better balance and sitting back on the skis when he came to a turn. He also used ski poles in an unorthodox way—to propel himself as he skied. The explosive new style helped cut Killy's racing time dramatically. In 1966 and 1967 he captured virtually every major skiing trophy. The next year he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics, a record in ski racing that has never been topped.
Killy learned an important secret shared by many creative people: innovations don't require genius, just a willingness to question the way things have always been done.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Scientific experiments have demonstrated incredible ways to kill a guinea pig, a small furry animal. Emotional upsets generate powerful and deadly toxic substances. Blood samples taken from persons experiencing intense fear or anger when injected into guinea pigs have killed them in less than two minutes. Imagine what these poisonous substances can do to your own body.
Every thought that you have affects your body chemistry within a split second. Remember how you feel when you're speeding down the highway and a big truck suddenly brakes twenty meters in front of you. A shockwave shoots through your whole system. Your mind produces instant reactions in your body.
The toxic substances that fear, anger, frustration, and stress produce not only kill guinea pigs but kill us off in a similar manner. It is impossible to be fearful, anxious, irritated, and healthy at the same time. It is not just difficult, it is impossible.
Simply put, your body's health is a reflection of your mental health. Sickness will often then be a result of unresolved inner conflicts which in time show up in the body.
It is also fascinating how our subconscious mind shapes our health. Do you recall feeling sick on a day when you didn't want to go to school? Headaches brought on by fear?
The mind-body connection is such that if, for example, we want to avoid something, very often our subconscious mind will arrange it. Once we recognize that these things happen to us, we are halfway to doing something about them.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Teachers and students alike have experienced the curious paradox that beginners, as a rule, tend to think too little about what they are doing because they think too much about what they are doing. Take, for example, people who are learning to play basketball or the piano. They have to give so much thought and attention to the low-level mechanics of handling the ball or fingering the keys or reading the music, that they are unable to give any thought to the thing that matters—the game, or the music, respectively.
With experts, it's just the other way around. They're open to the tactical possibilities and the musical challenges precisely because they're freed, through skill, from the need to pay attention to the low-level details of how to play. Indeed, when the expert pays attention to the mechanics, this is liable to disrupt performance.
This has led some to say that the expert operates in a zone "beyond thought", in a state of flow. But this is misleading. Expert performance is not beyond thought.
Smart basketball players or skilled musicians need to pay close attention to the demands of high performance, to the challenges to be overcome. What they don't need to do—what would be a distraction—is to have to think about where their fingers are, or how to control the ball while running. It's not mechanics, but the play itself, that absorbs the expert's intelligence.
A nice video published online last month sheds light on expertise and the conscious mind. The video reports a new study using an eye-tracking device.
It turns out that the less skilled pianist spends more time looking at her fingers than does the expert who, in contrast, is more likely to be looking at the sheet of music, or looking ahead at keys he's not yet playing. In general, the expert's gaze was calmer and more stable.
This is not a surprising finding. It supports what we might almost think of as conventional wisdom.
But it's remarkable for all that, nonetheless. The eye tracker gives expert and learning performers a glimpse into what they do without thinking about it.
The topic of the nature of skill—and the differences between beginners and experts—has been one of considerable discussion in cognitive science and philosophy.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Every summer when I top up my selection of summer outfits from the department stores, my eyes would nearly pop out of my head. I'm overwhelmed with a wide range of different slimming products each year. And more shockingly, these products are often advocated by very slim models.
Having lived in Asia for almost 10 years now, I've seen various dieting tips come and go. I remember in Japan, people heading directly to the fruit section in the supermarket, when the banana diet was at its peak. Then there was the black tea and oolong tea diet, followed by the soybean diet and the tomato juice diet. The list goes on and on.
Apart from what people eat, I've also seen many interesting slimming products. In Hong Kong, I've seen girls wrapping their whole body or both legs up with a special type of slimming tape which is supposed to help make them thinner. But it just reminded me of the roasted ham my mother usually puts on the dinner table at Christmas. Then there were the face slimming rollers that were said to improve your blood circulation and make your face smaller.
Personally I do not believe in any of these slimming gadgets and I think I have a very different perspective when it comes to the definition of what is beautiful. Asian women prefer to avoid the sun, because being pale or white is considered beautiful whereas a tanned complexion is considered much more beautiful and sexy in the West. It is most certainly shaped by a person's culture as well as how they were raised in their childhood.
As each summer season approaches, there's no escape from it. But it's not only women who are affected by this pressure to look good. Men aspire to be able to show off their 6 packs, or their v-shaped backs and there's a growing market of slimming pills aimed at men too.
I think no matter what diets we follow or what slimming products we obsess ourselves with, at the end of the day there's no magic trick to shape up for the summer. Eat in a balanced way and incorporate the right level of physical activity. For me, this still seems to be the best plan.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Skin may seem like a superficial human attribute, but it's the first thing we notice about anyone we meet. As a zoologist focusing on the studies of apes and monkeys, I've been studying why humans evolved to become the naked ape, and why skin comes in so many different shades around the world.
We can make a very good estimate from the fossil record that humans probably evolved naked skin around a million and a half years ago, and meanwhile they mostly lost their coat of fur. Today we have a few patches of hair remaining on various parts of our bodies, but compared with apes and monkeys, we have very little. Basically, we turned our skin darker to serve as a natural sun protector in the place of the hair we lost.
We think we lost this hair because of the need to keep ourselves cool when we were moving around vigorously in a hot environment. We can't really lose heat by breathing quickly and loudly like dogs. We have to do it by sweating. So we evolved the ability to sweat plentifully and lost most of our fur.
Most animals protect themselves from the sun with fur. What we did in our ancestry was to produce more permanent natural coloring in our skin cells.
This was really an important revolution in human history because it allowed us to continue to evolve in equatorial environments. It really made it possible for us to continue along the path toward modern humans in Africa.
For most of human history we all had dark skin. What we see today is the product of evolutionary events resulting from the dispersal of a few human populations out of Africa around 60,000 to 70,000 years ago.
Our species originated around 200,000 years ago and underwent tremendous diversification—culturally, technologically, linguistically, artistically—for 130,000 years. After that, a few small populations left Africa to populate the rest of the world. These early ancestors of modern Eurasians dispersed into parts of the world that had more seasonal sunshine and much lower levels of sun radiation. It's in these populations that we begin to see real changes in the genetic makeup of natural coloring.
Today, skin color is evolving via new mixtures of people coming together and having children with new mixtures of skin color genes. We can see this in almost every large city worldwide. Not only the coloring genes, but lots of other genes are getting mixed up, too.

questions.prompt: What did Cathy and Brenda finish doing last week?
options: A six-month-long negotiation.
Preparations for the party.
A project with a troublesome client.
Gift wrapping for the colleagues.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Cathy and Brenda finish doing last week? 

 【翻译】 Cathy和Brenda上周完成了什么? 
 A)  一场为期六个月的谈判。 
 B)  聚会的准备工作。 
 C)  一个麻烦客户的项目。 
 D)  给同事们包装礼物。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） A project with a troublesome client. 
 【定位】 P3 We just wrapped up a project with a difficult client last week. 
 我们上周刚刚搞定了一个难缠客户的项目。 

 【信号】 完成信号 wrapped up 加时间 last week 。We just wrapped up a project with a difficult client last week. 里 wrapped up 是『完成、收尾』的强信号，又精确带上 last week，与题干时间对上，这一句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 wrapped up a project with a difficult client ↔ A project with a troublesome client 同义改写 difficult=troublesome 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 A six-month-long negotiation. 里的 six-month 看似呼应原文 We've only been working together the last six months，但 six months 说的是两人共事的时长，不是上周做完的事，更没有 negotiation（谈判）一词，是把听到的数字硬安到本题上的原词陷阱。  借用原文：We've only been working together the last six months 

 B) 原词陷阱 Preparations for the party. 借了原文 she can focus on wedding preparations 里的 preparations，但原文是说 Brenda 接下来要忙婚礼筹备，并非上周已完成的事，时间和归属都不对。  借用原文：she can focus on wedding preparations 

 D) 原词陷阱 Gift wrapping for the colleagues. 利用了原文 wrapped up 的 wrap 字面，制造『包装礼物 gift wrapping』的联想，但录音从未提到给同事包装礼物，纯属字面误导。  借用原文：We just wrapped up a project

questions.prompt: What is John going to do for Brenda?
options: Take wedding photos.
Advertise her company.
Start a small business.
Throw a celebration party.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is John going to do for Brenda? 

 【翻译】 John打算为Brenda做什么? 
 A)  拍摄婚礼照片。 
 B)  为她的公司做广告。 
 C)  创办一家小企业。 
 D)  举办一场庆祝聚会。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Take wedding photos. 
 【定位】 P6 I'll actually be taking photos during the big event as a wedding gift. 
 婚礼当天我其实会负责拍照，作为送给新人的结婚礼物。 

 【信号】 将来式 I'll be 自述要做的事 。I'll actually be taking photos during the big event as a wedding gift 用将来进行时 I'll be taking 由 John 本人说出自己届时要做的事，是『某人打算做什么』的直接应答信号。 

 【替换】 taking photos during the big event ↔ Take wedding photos 概括替换 the big event=wedding 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Advertise her company. 借了原文 I worked in advertising for a while，但那是 John 大学毕业后的旧工作，且 advertising 是行业、不是为 Brenda 做广告，时间与对象都错。  借用原文：I worked in advertising for a while 

 C) 原词陷阱 Start a small business. 来自 I turned my photography hobby into a small business，但那是 John 已经做成的事、是他自己的事业，不是他要『为 Brenda』做的，张冠了对象。  借用原文：I turned my photography hobby into a small business 

 D) 未提及 Throw a celebration party. 借派对场景做联想，但录音里没有任何人说要为 Brenda 办庆祝派对，John 要做的是拍照，纯属未提及。

questions.prompt: How did Cathy feel when asked to bake the cake?
options: Hesitant.
Nervous.
Flattered.
Surprised.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did Cathy feel when asked to bake the cake? 

 【翻译】 当被要求烤制蛋糕时,Cathy感觉如何? 
 A)  犹豫的。 
 B)  紧张的。 
 C)  受宠若惊的。 
 D)  惊讶的。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） Nervous. 
 【定位】 P7 I was a bit nervous saying yes, because I'm far from a professional. 
 我答应的时候有点紧张，因为我离专业水准还差得远。 

 【信号】 情绪自陈 a bit nervous 加原因 。I was a bit nervous saying yes, because I'm far from a professional 里 Cathy 直接说出 nervous，并用 because 解释紧张原因，是态度的直接自陈信号。 

 【替换】 I was a bit nervous ↔ Nervous 原词直陈即态度 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 Hesitant. 表犹豫，与紧张方向相近易混，但 Cathy 是 nervous saying yes——她最终答应了，并未表现出迟疑不决，原文没有犹豫的依据。  借用原文：I was a bit nervous saying yes 

 C) 未提及 Flattered. 指受到抬举而高兴，但原文 because I'm far from a professional 透出的是担心自己不够专业，并无被恭维的得意之情，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 Surprised. 借了原文 I was a little surprised to be invited，但 surprised 说的是 Cathy 对『被邀请参加派对』感到意外，不是对『被请求做蛋糕』的感受，被问的那件事换了，情绪原词便对不上本题。  借用原文：I was a little surprised to be invited

questions.prompt: What does the man suggest the woman do?
options: Start her own bakery.
Improve her baking skill.
Share her cooking experience.
Prepare for the wedding
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man suggest the woman do? 

 【翻译】 男士建议女士做什么? 
 A)  开办她自己的面包店。 
 B)  提高她的烘焙技能。 
 C)  分享她的烹饪经验。 
 D)  为婚礼做准备。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Start her own bakery. 
 【定位】 P12 with your event planning experience, you could very well open your own shop. 
 凭你的活动策划经验，你完全可以开一家属于自己的店。 

 【信号】 建议句式 you could very well 。you could very well open your own shop 用 you could 这一典型建议句式，由男方对女方说出，是『建议做什么』的直接信号。 

 【替换】 open your own shop ↔ Start her own bakery 具体化替换 shop=bakery 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 Improve her baking skill. 围绕 baking 做合理联想，但男方夸她 You're a natural 已是天赋型选手，并未建议她去提升手艺，原文没有这层意思。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Share her cooking experience. 借了原文 with your event planning experience 的 experience，但原文是说凭经验去开店，并非建议她去『分享』经验，动作被偷换。  借用原文：with your event planning experience 

 D) 原词陷阱 Prepare for the wedding 利用全程的婚礼话题，但男方的建议是开店，并非让她去筹备婚礼；筹备婚礼是背景事件，不是男方提出的建议，属未提及的建议。  借用原文：with your event planning experience, you could very well open your own shop

questions.prompt: What does the man say about college students as compared with high schoolers?
options: They have to spend more time studying.
They have to participate in club activities.
They have to be more responsible for what they do.
They have to choose a specific academic discipline.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about college students as compared with high schoolers? 

 【翻译】 与高中生相比，这位男士对大学生有何看法? 
 A)  他们必须花更多时间学习。 
 B)  他们必须参加社团活动。 
 C)  他们必须对自己的行为更加负责。 
 D)  他们必须选择一个具体的学术学科。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They have to be more responsible for what they do. 
 【定位】 P3 Many aspects are different here at university. The most important one is that you have to take more individual responsibility for your actions. 
 大学里很多方面都不一样。其中最重要的一点是，你必须为自己的行为承担更多的个人责任。 

 【信号】 最高级 the most important 点睛 。男方先说 Many aspects are different，紧接着用最高级 The most important one is 把众多不同里"最重要的"那条单拎出来——最高级之后就是答案句，他要强调的正是"承担更多个人责任"。 

 【替换】 take more individual responsibility for your actions ↔ be more responsible for what they do 名词转形容词的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里反复出现 study（how much effort you put into study），A 项 spend more time studying 正是盗用这个原词；但原文说的是"投入多少由你的自律决定"，并非"必须花更多时间学习"，听到 study 就选会中招。  借用原文：how much effort you put into study 

 B) 答非所问 B 项 participate in club activities 里的 club activities 出现在后文第 9 段，是第 8 题讨论的内容，与第 5 题"最重要的不同"无关；且原文是说"不该花太多时间在社团"，更非"必须参加"。  借用原文：there are a lot of wonderful clubs 

 D) 未提及 D 项 choose a specific academic discipline（选一门具体专业）听上去很像大学场景该有的事，但录音从头到尾没说要"选专业"，属凭常识脑补、原文无据。

questions.prompt: What are college students expected to do according to the man?
options: Get ready for a career.
Make a lot of friends.
Set a long-term goal.
Behave like adults.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are college students expected to do according to the man? 

 【翻译】 根据这位男士的说法，大学生应该做什么? 
 A)  为职业生涯做好准备。 
 B)  结交很多朋友。 
 C)  设定一个长远目标。 
 D)  表现得像成年人一样。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Behave like adults. 
 【定位】 P5 It's just that suddenly at university you are expected to behave like an adult, that means concentrating on the direction of your life in general and your own academic performance specifically. 
 只是说，到了大学你突然就被期望像个成年人一样行事，也就是说，总体上要专注于自己人生的方向，具体来说要专注于自己的学业表现。 

 【信号】 被问者应答里的 expected to 。女方追问"Nobody cares, you mean?"，男方的应答里出现 you are expected to behave like an adult，正用题干同款词 expected to——被问者的直接应答 + 题干原词双重信号，锁定此句。 

 【替换】 behave like an adult ↔ Behave like adults. 近乎原句的同义对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 Get ready for a career. 是大学常被联想的目标，但录音里男方谈的是"像成年人一样行事、专注人生方向和学业"，并没说"为就业做准备"，属常识脑补。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音后文确有 You will make interesting friends，B 项 Make a lot of friends. 盗用了 friends；但那是第 7 题讲交友、且原文强调"只留尊重学业的朋友"，并非"被期望多交朋友"。  借用原文：You will make interesting friends 

 C) 偷换概念 录音说 concentrating on the direction of your life（专注人生方向），C 项 Set a long-term goal.（设定长期目标）把"方向"偷换成"设目标"，看似相近实则不是一回事，原文没说要"设定目标"。  借用原文：concentrating on the direction of your life

questions.prompt: What kind of friends does the man suggest the woman make as a college student?
options: Those who share her academic interests.
Those who respect her student commitments.
Those who can help her when she is in need.
Those who go to the same clubs as she does.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What kind of friends does the man suggest the woman make as a college student? 

 【翻译】 这位男士建议这位女士作为大学生应该结交什么样的朋友? 
 A)  那些与她有共同学术兴趣的人。 
 B)  那些尊重她学业责任的人。 
 C)  那些能在她需要时帮助她的人。 
 D)  那些和她去同样社团的人。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Those who respect her student commitments. 
 【定位】 P9 You will make interesting friends, but you need only keep the friends who respect your student commitments. 
 你会结识有趣的朋友，但你只需保留那些尊重你学生本分的朋友。 

 【信号】 转折 but 之后才是真意 。前半 You will make interesting friends 是铺垫，转折词 but 之后 keep the friends who respect your student commitments 才是男方真正的建议——but 后是答案句，前半句是用来干扰"听到 friends 就选"的人。 

 【替换】 keep the friends who respect your student commitments ↔ Those who respect her student commitments. 人称转换的同义对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 share her academic interests 把"学业"和"兴趣"拼在一起，听上去合理，但录音说的是"尊重你学生本分"，从未提"志趣相投"，属脑补。 
 C) 未提及 C 项 help her when she is in need（在她需要时能帮她的人）是对"好朋友"的常识定义，但录音的标准是"尊重学业"，与"能帮忙"无关，原文无据。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音后句确有 there are a lot of wonderful clubs，D 项 go to the same clubs as she does 盗用 clubs；但 clubs 是讲社团时间分配（第 8 题）的，男方从没说"和同社团的人交友"，听到 clubs 就选正中陷阱。  借用原文：there are a lot of wonderful clubs

questions.prompt: What kind of club activities should college students engage in according to the man?
options: Those helpful for tapping their potential.
Those conducive to improving their social skills.
Those helpful for cultivating individual interests.
Those conducive to their academic studies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What kind of club activities should college students engage in according to the man? 

 【翻译】 根据这位男士的说法，大学生应该参加什么样的社团活动? 
 A)  那些有助于发掘他们潜力的活动。 
 B)  那些有利于提高他们社交技能的活动。 
 C)  那些有助于培养个人兴趣的活动。 
 D)  那些有利于他们学业的活动。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Those conducive to their academic studies. 
 【定位】 P9 Also, there are a lot of wonderful clubs, but you shouldn't allocate too much time to club activities, unless they are directly related to your study. 
 另外，社团很多很棒，但你不该在社团活动上分配太多时间，除非它们与你的学业直接相关。 

 【信号】 unless 引出唯一例外 。男方先说"不该花太多时间在社团"，再用 unless they are directly related to your study 给出唯一例外——unless 后的条件就是"什么样的社团可以参加"，是答案句的灵魂。 

 【替换】 directly related to your study ↔ Those conducive to their academic studies. related to=conducive to 的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 helpful for tapping their potential（有助发掘潜能）是社团活动常被说的好处，听上去合理，但录音的唯一标准是"与学业相关"，未提潜能，属脑补。 
 B) 未提及 B 项 conducive to improving their social skills（有助提升社交能力）也是社团的常见联想好处，但录音只说"与学业相关"才值得花时间，没提社交，原文无据。 
 C) 偷换概念 C 项 helpful for cultivating individual interests（有助培养个人兴趣）与 D 的"学业相关"形成正面对立；录音明说标准是"与学业相关"，C 把"学业"偷换成"个人兴趣"，方向相反。  借用原文：directly related to your study

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most successful people?
options: They break away from traditional ways of thinking.
They are prepared to work harder than anyone else.
They are good at refining old formulas.
They bring their potential into full play.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about most successful people? 

 【翻译】 说话者对大多数成功人士有何评价? 
 A)  他们打破了传统的思维方式。 
 B)  他们准备比任何人都更加努力地工作。 
 C)  他们善于改进旧有的方法。 
 D)  他们充分发挥了自己的潜能。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They break away from traditional ways of thinking. 
 【定位】 P1 Most successful people are unorthodox persons whose minds wander outside traditional ways of thinking. Instead of trying to refine old formulas, they invent new ones. 
 大多数成功者都是不循常规的人，他们的思维游走于传统思维方式之外。他们不去改良旧公式，而是发明新公式。 

 【信号】 总括句+Instead of 取舍信号 。录音开篇就是对成功者的总括，并用 Instead of trying to refine old formulas, they invent new ones 中的 Instead of 给出明确取舍——'不是改良旧的、而是发明新的'，这个'不是A而是B'的信号直接点出成功者的本质特征，就是答案句。 

 【替换】 minds wander outside traditional ways of thinking ↔ break away from traditional ways of thinking wander outside ≈ break away from（跳出传统） 
 they invent new ones ↔ break away from traditional ways of thinking '发明新的'佐证'打破传统' 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 They are prepared to work harder than anyone else. 的措辞几乎照搬第 2 段 he was prepared to work harder than anyone else，听到原话极易选；但那句讲的是 Killy 个人一开始的做法，且后文紧接 simply training harder would never be enough（光苦练远远不够），说明'更努力'恰恰不是成功者的关键共性，答非所问。  借用原文：he was prepared to work harder than anyone else 

 C) 与原文相反 They are good at refining old formulas. 直接挪用录音 Instead of trying to refine old formulas 里的 refine old formulas；但原文是用 Instead of 把'改良旧公式'否定掉、说成功者偏偏不这么做，选项却说他们'擅长改良旧公式'，正好与原文相反。  借用原文：Instead of trying to refine old formulas 

 D) 未提及 They bring their potential into full play. 听起来像成功学套话，但录音通篇讲的是'跳出传统、发明新法'，从没提到'发挥潜能（potential）'这层意思，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about Killy's experiments?
options: They contributed to the popularity of skiing worldwide.
They resulted in a brand-new style of skiing techniques.
They promoted the scientific use of skiing poles.
They made explosive news in the sports world.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about Killy's experiments? 

 【翻译】 说话者对Killy的实验有何评价? 
 A)  它们促进了滑雪运动在全世界的普及。 
 B)  它们产生了一种全新的滑雪技术风格。 
 C)  它们推动了滑雪杖的科学使用。 
 D)  它们在体育界引起了爆炸性新闻。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They resulted in a brand-new style of skiing techniques. 
 【定位】 P3 His experiments resulted in a new style that was almost exactly opposite the accepted technique of the time. 
 他的实验催生了一种全新风格，几乎与当时公认的技术完全相反。 

 【信号】 因果信号 resulted in 直引出结果 。录音 His experiments resulted in a new style 里的 resulted in 是明确的因果信号词，experiments 是因、紧跟的 a new style 就是要找的果，信号词后面的内容直接就是答案句。 

 【替换】 resulted in a new style ↔ resulted in a brand-new style of skiing techniques new style ≈ brand-new style of skiing techniques 
 almost exactly opposite the accepted technique of the time ↔ a brand-new style of skiing techniques '与公认技术相反'强化了'全新' 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 They contributed to the popularity of skiing worldwide. 把实验的影响夸大为'让滑雪在全世界流行'；录音只说实验催生了新风格、帮 Killy 自己缩短了比赛时间，从未说它让滑雪运动在全球流行，属过度推断/放大范围。 
 C) 偷换概念 They promoted the scientific use of skiing poles. 挪用了录音 He also used ski poles in an unorthodox way 里的 ski poles；但原文说他是'用非常规的方式（unorthodox way）'用雪杖来助推，根本不是'科学使用（scientific use）'，把'非常规'偷换成了'科学'。  借用原文：He also used ski poles in an unorthodox way 

 D) 原词陷阱 They made explosive news in the sports world. 抓住了录音里很扎眼的 explosive 一词；但原文 The explosive new style helped cut Killy's racing time 里 explosive 修饰的是'new style（爆发式的新风格）'，讲它大幅缩短了比赛时间，根本没说'造成爆炸性新闻'，原词被挪了搭配。  借用原文：The explosive new style helped cut Killy's racing time

questions.prompt: What is said to be Killy's biggest honor in his skiing career?
options: He was recognized as a genius in the world of sports.
He competed in all major skiing events in the world.
He won three gold medals in one Winter Olympics.
He broke three world skiing records in three years.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said to be Killy's biggest honor in his skiing career? 

 【翻译】 Killy滑雪生涯中最大的荣誉是什么? 
 A)  他被公认为体育界的天才。 
 B)  他参加了世界上所有主要的滑雪赛事。 
 C)  他在一届冬季奥运会上赢得了三枚金牌。 
 D)  他在三年内打破了三项世界滑雪纪录。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） He won three gold medals in one Winter Olympics. 
 【定位】 P3 The next year he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics, a record in ski racing that has never been topped. 
 第二年他在冬奥会上赢得三枚金牌，这是滑雪比赛中一项从未被超越的纪录。 

 【信号】 数字+最高级 never been topped 。录音 he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics, a record in ski racing that has never been topped 同时给了硬数字（three gold medals）和最高级评价（never been topped 从未被超越），'从未被超越'正是'最大荣誉'的信号，定为答案句。 

 【替换】 he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics ↔ He won three gold medals in one Winter Olympics. 几乎原句对应，only 'the'→'one' 
 a record in ski racing that has never been topped ↔ He won three gold medals in one Winter Olympics. '从未被超越的纪录'印证这是最大荣誉 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 He was recognized as a genius in the world of sports. 利用了第 4 段 innovations don't require genius 里的 genius；但原文恰恰说'创新不需要天才'，是在否定'天才'这一前提，选项却说他'被公认为天才'，与原文意思相反，且这不是在讲荣誉。  借用原文：innovations don't require genius 

 B) 偷换概念 He competed in all major skiing events in the world. 听上去呼应录音 he captured virtually every major skiing trophy；但原文说的是'夺得几乎每一项重大滑雪奖杯（captured trophy）'，是'拿奖'不是'参加（competed in）所有赛事'，把'夺奖'偷换成'参赛'，且 all 比原文 virtually every 更绝对。  借用原文：he captured virtually every major skiing trophy 

 D) 原词陷阱 He broke three world skiing records in three years. 抓住录音里的数字 three 与年份信息（1966、1967、the next year）东拼西凑出'三年破三项世界纪录'；但原文是 In 1966 and 1967 he captured virtually every major skiing trophy 讲夺奖、次年 he won three gold medals 讲三金，'three'配的是金牌不是纪录，更没说'破三项世界纪录'，数字张冠李戴。  借用原文：he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics

questions.prompt: What happens to guinea pigs, when blood samples of angry people are injected into them?
options: They appear restless.
They lose consciousness.
They become upset.
They die almost instantly.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What happens to guinea pigs, when blood samples of angry people are injected into them? 

 【翻译】 当愤怒者的血液样本被注射到豚鼠体内时,豚鼠会发生什么? 
 A)  它们显得焦躁不安。 
 B)  它们失去意识。 
 C)  它们变得烦躁。 
 D)  它们几乎立即死亡。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They die almost instantly. 
 【定位】 P1 Blood samples taken from persons experiencing intense fear or anger when injected into guinea pigs have killed them in less than two minutes. 
 从经历强烈恐惧或愤怒的人身上抽取的血样，注入豚鼠体内后，在不到两分钟内就把它们杀死了。 

 【信号】 结果动词 killed 即结局落点 。这句出现强结果动词 killed them in less than two minutes，killed 直接交代了豚鼠的最终结局，是承载答案的关键动作词，听到它就锁定这一句。 

 【替换】 killed them in less than two minutes ↔ They die almost instantly. 致死改写为致死，时长改写为副词 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They appear restless. 说豚鼠"显得不安"，远轻于录音的 killed，把致命结局偷换成轻微反应；录音从未提及豚鼠"不安"，属程度被改轻的无中生有。 
 B) 偷换概念 They lose consciousness.（失去意识）听上去与"被注射后出事"沾边，但录音明说的是 killed them（被杀死），死亡比昏迷重一档；选项偷偷把"死"降成"昏迷"。  借用原文：killed them in less than two minutes 

 C) 原词陷阱 They become upset. 里的 upset 正是录音里反复出现的原词 Emotional upsets，但那是形容"人的情绪波动"产生毒素，不是说豚鼠"变得难受"；选项盗用 upset 制造"听到就想选"的错觉。  借用原文：Emotional upsets generate powerful and deadly toxic substances

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about every thought you have?
options: It has an instant effect on your body chemistry.
It keeps returning to you every now and then.
It leaves you with a long lasting impression.
It contributes to the shaping of your mind.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about every thought you have? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于你的每一个想法说了什么? 
 A)  它对你的身体化学反应有即时影响。 
 B)  它时不时地再次出现在你脑海中。 
 C)  它给你留下持久的印象。 
 D)  它有助于塑造你的思维。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It has an instant effect on your body chemistry. 
 【定位】 P2 Every thought that you have affects your body chemistry within a split second. 
 你产生的每一个念头，都会在一瞬间影响你的身体化学反应。 

 【信号】 时间词 within a split second 即时效落点 。题干对象 thought 一出现，紧跟的判定就是 affects your body chemistry within a split second，其中"a split second（一瞬间）"正是预读锁定的时效维度落点，听到它即定位本句。 

 【替换】 affects your body chemistry within a split second ↔ It has an instant effect on your body chemistry. 动词改名词、瞬间换同义词 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It keeps returning to you every now and then. 说念头"时不时回来"，与录音强调的"瞬间作用于身体"无关，录音没说念头会反复回返，属无中生有。 
 C) 与原文相反 It leaves you with a long lasting impression. 的"long lasting（持久）"恰与录音的 within a split second（瞬间）在时间维度上相反；选项取了与原文相反的极性。  借用原文：within a split second 

 D) 张冠李戴 It contributes to the shaping of your mind. 谈的是"塑造心智"，方向是"心智被塑"；而本段说的是念头作用于 body chemistry（身体），作用对象被掉了个；"塑造"相关内容其实在后文谈 subconscious 时才出现，安到本题即张冠李戴。  借用原文：how our subconscious mind shapes our health

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about every thought you have?
options: To succeed while feeling irritated.
To feel happy without good health.
To be free from frustration and failure.
To enjoy good health while in dark moods.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about every thought you have? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于你的每一个想法说了什么? 
 A)  在感到恼怒的同时取得成功。 
 B)  在没有良好健康的情况下感到快乐。 
 C)  摆脱挫折和失败。 
 D)  在阴郁情绪中享有良好健康。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） To enjoy good health while in dark moods. 
 【定位】 P3 It is impossible to be fearful, anxious, irritated, and healthy at the same time. It is not just difficult, it is impossible. 
 一个人不可能在恐惧、焦虑、烦躁的同时又保持健康。这不只是困难，而是根本不可能。 

 【信号】 强判定词 impossible 加重复强调 。这句以 It is impossible 作判定，并用 It is not just difficult, it is impossible 重复加重语气，强调正是答案句的信号——说话人反复强调处即考点。 

 【替换】 impossible to be fearful, anxious, irritated, and healthy at the same time ↔ To enjoy good health while in dark moods. 负面情绪概括为 dark moods，并存关系保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To succeed while feeling irritated. 里 irritated 取自原文 irritated，但 succeed（成功）原文从未提及；选项盗用 irritated 一词，再拼上无中生有的"成功"。  借用原文：fearful, anxious, irritated 

 B) 偷换概念 To feel happy without good health. 谈"没有健康却快乐"，方向与原文"坏情绪 vs 健康不能并存"对不上：原文说的是"坏情绪伴健康不可能"，不是"无健康却快乐"，逻辑被掉换。 
 C) 原词陷阱 To be free from frustration and failure. 里 frustration 取自原文 frustration，但"摆脱挫折与失败"是录音没有下过的判断，选项盗用 frustration 制造熟悉感。  借用原文：fear, anger, frustration, and stress produce

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about our mind and body?
options: They are closely connected.
They function in a similar way.
They are too complex to understand.
They are too complex to understand.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about our mind and body? 

 【翻译】 这段话关于我们的思维和身体说了什么? 
 A)  它们紧密相连。 
 B)  它们以相似的方式运作。 
 C)  它们过于复杂而难以理解。 
 D)  它们过于复杂而难以理解。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are closely connected. 
 【定位】 P6 The mind-body connection is such that if, for example, we want to avoid something, very often our subconscious mind will arrange it. 
 心身之间的关联是这样的：比如当我们想回避某件事时，潜意识常常会替我们把它安排出来。 

 【信号】 关系名词 connection 直接点题 。这句以 The mind-body connection 把心智与身体直接捆在一起命名为"关联"，connection 就是两者关系的总括落点；本段 your body's health is a reflection of your mental health 亦呼应同一结论。 

 【替换】 The mind-body connection ↔ They are closely connected. 名词 connection 还原为形容词 connected 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 They function in a similar way. 说两者"运作方式相似"，而录音说的是"相互关联（connection）"，相连不等于运作相似；选项把"关联"偷换成"相似"这种另一种关系。 
 C) 未提及 They are too complex to understand. 说两者"复杂到难以理解"，但录音通篇在阐明两者如何相连、还说 we are halfway to doing something about them（我们已离解决问题不远），态度是"可认识、可处理"，并非"难懂"，属无中生有且基调相反。 
 D) 未提及 They are too complex to understand. 与 C 内容完全相同，同样把两者说成"复杂难懂"，与录音"相连且可处理"的结论不符，理由同 C。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about beginners and expert pianists?
options: They differ in their appreciation of music.
They focus their attention on different things.
They finger the piano keys in different ways.
They choose different pieces of music to play.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about beginners and expert pianists? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于初学者和专业钢琴家说了什么? 
 A)  他们对音乐的欣赏不同。 
 B)  他们关注的事物不同。 
 C)  他们按琴键的方式不同。 
 D)  他们选择演奏不同的曲目。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They focus their attention on different things. 
 【定位】 P1 They have to give so much thought and attention to the low-level mechanics of handling the ball or fingering the keys or reading the music, that they are unable to give any thought to the thing that matters—the game, or the music, respectively. With experts, it's just the other way around. They're open to the tactical possibilities and the musical challenges precisely because they're freed, through skill, from the need to pay attention to the low-level details. 
 新手必须把大量心思和注意力放在按球、按琴键、读谱这些低层次的机械动作上，以至于无暇去想真正要紧的东西——比赛本身或音乐本身。而专家恰恰相反：正因为靠技能从关注低层细节中解放出来，他们能把心思放在战术可能性与音乐挑战上。 

 【信号】 对比信号 the other way around 。新手那句强调注意力在 the low-level mechanics，紧接着第 2 段 With experts, it's just the other way around（恰恰相反）这一对比信号点明两类人注意力放的位置正相反，正反对照处就是答案句。 

 【替换】 give so much thought and attention to the low-level mechanics ↔ focus their attention on different things "注意力放在低层机械"被概括为"注意力放在不同东西上" 
 it's just the other way around ↔ different things "正相反"对应"不同" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 用了录音反复出现的 music，但录音说的是两类人"注意力落点"不同，从没说他们对音乐的 appreciation（欣赏/鉴赏）不同，是借 music 一词答非所问。  借用原文：reading the music 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 抓住录音里很具体的 fingering the keys，但原文是说新手"得分心去 finger the keys"、专家不必，讲的是注意力，并非说两人"指法方式不同"，属偷换概念。  借用原文：fingering the keys 

 D) 未提及 D 用了 pieces of music/play，但录音通篇没提两类人"选不同曲子弹"，纯属拿熟词拼出的未提及内容。  借用原文：the music

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the new study published in an online video?
options: It marks a breakthrough in behavioral science.
It adopts a conventional approach to research.
It supports a piece of conventional wisdom.
It gives rise to controversy among experts.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the new study published in an online video? 

 【翻译】 关于发表在在线视频中的新研究,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它标志着行为科学的突破。 
 B)  它采用传统的研究方法。 
 C)  它支持一条传统智慧。 
 D)  它在专家中引起争议。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It supports a piece of conventional wisdom. 
 【定位】 P7 This is not a surprising finding. It supports what we might almost think of as conventional wisdom. 
 这并不是一个令人惊讶的发现。它印证了我们几乎可以视为常识的东西。 

 【信号】 定性信号 supports…conventional wisdom 。第 7 段先用 not a surprising finding 定调"不意外"，再直接说 It supports what we might almost think of as conventional wisdom，supports + conventional wisdom 就是对研究的定性，是答案句。 

 【替换】 It supports what we might almost think of as conventional wisdom ↔ It supports a piece of conventional wisdom 近乎原句，只把从句压成名词短语 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说这是 breakthrough（突破），但录音明确说 not a surprising finding（并不令人惊讶），"不意外"与"突破"正相反，属与原文相反兼过度拔高。  借用原文：This is not a surprising finding 

 B) 与原文相反 B 说研究"用了常规/老套方法"，但录音说它用的是 a new study using an eye-tracking device（眼动仪），是新手段而非 conventional approach，与原文相反。  借用原文：a new study using an eye-tracking device 

 D) 未提及 D 说研究"在专家中引发争议"，但录音对该发现的定性是"不意外、印证常识"，根本没提任何争议，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What overwhelms the speaker when she buys her summer outfits each year?
options: People's envy of slim models.
People's craze for good health.
The increasing range of fancy products.
The great variety of slimming products.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What overwhelms the speaker when she buys her summer outfits each year? 

 【翻译】 说话者每年购买夏季服装时,什么让她感到不知所措? 
 A)  人们对苗条模特的羡慕。 
 B)  人们对健康的狂热追求。 
 C)  花哨产品的种类日益增多。 
 D)  减肥产品的种类繁多。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The great variety of slimming products. 
 【定位】 P1 I'm overwhelmed with a wide range of different slimming products each year. 
 每年我都被五花八门、种类繁多的减肥瘦身产品弄得不知所措。 

 【信号】 题干原词 overwhelmed 在录音中直接落点 。录音 I'm overwhelmed with a wide range of different slimming products 里的 overwhelmed 正是题干的提问词，这种"题干提问词在原文原样出现"的句子就是答案句的强信号，紧跟其后的 a wide range of different slimming products 就是答案对象。 

 【替换】 a wide range of different slimming products ↔ The great variety of slimming products a wide range of different = The great variety of 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音末句确实提到 very slim models，A 项 People's envy of slim models. 借这个 slim models 引诱你"听到就选"，但录音只说产品由瘦模特代言，从未说人们"羡慕(envy)"模特，envy 是无中生有。  借用原文：very slim models 

 B) 偷换概念 录音通篇讲减肥产品，结尾才提 Eat in a balanced way 的健康主张，但 19 题问的是"买夏装时被什么震到"，B 项 People's craze for good health. 既不在答案句、又把对象偷换成"健康狂热"，答非所问。 
 C) 偷换概念 C 项 The increasing range of fancy products. 与正确项句式几乎一样（都说"产品种类多"），但把 slimming 换成了 fancy（花哨的）。录音说的是 slimming products（减肥产品），从未说 fancy products，这一字之差就是错点。  借用原文：slimming products

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think of girls wrapping their legs up with slimming tape?
options: They appear vigorous.
They appear strange.
They look charming.
They look unhealthy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker think of girls wrapping their legs up with slimming tape? 

 【翻译】 说话者如何看待女孩们用瘦身胶带缠绕腿部? 
 A)  她们显得精力充沛。 
 B)  她们显得奇怪。 
 C)  她们看起来很有魅力。 
 D)  她们看起来不健康。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） They appear strange. 
 【定位】 P3 In Hong Kong, I've seen girls wrapping their whole body or both legs up with a special type of slimming tape which is supposed to help make them thinner. But it just reminded me of the roasted ham my mother usually puts on the dinner table at Christmas. 
 在香港，我见过女孩们用一种据说能让人变瘦的特制塑身胶带把全身或双腿缠起来。但这只让我联想到我母亲圣诞节常端上餐桌的烤火腿。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后的比喻才是真态度 。前半句客观描述"用胶带缠腿"，But it just reminded me of the roasted ham 用 But 转折，后面把缠腿的样子比作"烤火腿"，转折后的这个比喻才暴露说话人的真实评价——觉得样子怪异、滑稽。 

 【替换】 it just reminded me of the roasted ham ↔ They appear strange. 把人腿比作烤火腿=觉得样子怪 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 项 They appear vigorous.（显得有活力）是正面评价，但录音用 But 转折后把缠腿比作火腿，态度是负面/觉得怪，方向相反。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音前半提到胶带 supposed to help make them thinner（据说能变瘦），C 项 They look charming.（显得迷人）顺着"变瘦=好看"的常识把人引向正面评价，但说话人本人的评价是火腿比喻的"怪"，charming 是被常识带偏的误判。  借用原文：supposed to help make them thinner 

 D) 过度推断 D 项 They look unhealthy.（显得不健康）看似贴合"减肥"话题，但录音的火腿比喻表达的是"样子怪"，并没说"看起来不健康"；把 strange 推到 unhealthy 是多走了一步的过度推断。

【题目】 What does the speaker think affects people's interpretation of beauty? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为什么影响了人们对美的诠释? 
 A)  文化和教养。

 这（对美的看法）无疑是由一个人的文化以及他们童年时的成长方式所塑造的。 

 【信号】 因果信号 shaped by 后接成因 。It is most certainly shaped by a person's culture as well as how they were raised in their childhood 里的 shaped by 是明确的归因信号，most certainly 又加重了语气，shaped by 后面紧跟的 culture 与 how they were raised 就是答案。 

 【替换】 a person's culture ↔ Culture and upbringing. a person's culture = Culture 
 how they were raised in their childhood ↔ Culture and upbringing. how they were raised in childhood = upbringing 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 B 项 Wealth and social status. 听上去像合理成因，但录音的归因句只说 culture 和 childhood，从头到尾没提财富或社会地位，属无中生有。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音第 5 段确有 this pressure to look good 和"男性也受影响"，C 项 Peer pressure. 借这个 pressure 引诱选，但那讲的是"想变好看的压力"，而非"什么塑造了审美标准"，且原文是 pressure 不是 peer pressure，答非所问。  借用原文：this pressure to look good 

 D) 过度推断 录音开头提到产品由 very slim models 代言，让人联想到媒体影响，D 项 Media influence. 正利用这种联想，但归因句明确说是 culture 与 upbringing，从未把审美归于媒体，属过度推断。  借用原文：very slim models

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mainly talk about?
options: The relation between hair and skin.
The growing interest in skin studies.
The color of human skin.
The need of skin protection.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker mainly talk about? 

 【翻译】 说话者主要谈论什么? 
 A)  毛发与皮肤的关系。 
 B)  对皮肤研究日益增长的兴趣。 
 C)  人类皮肤的颜色。 
 D)  皮肤保护的需要。 

 【答案】 C （主旨题） The color of human skin. 
 【定位】 P1 As a zoologist focusing on the studies of apes and monkeys, I've been studying why humans evolved to become the naked ape, and why skin comes in so many different shades around the world. 
 作为一名专注研究猿和猴的动物学家，我一直在研究人类为何进化成了裸猿，以及为何全世界人类的肤色会有如此多不同的深浅。 

 【信号】 开头自述研究方向即点题 。讲者用 I've been studying why humans evolved to become the naked ape, and why skin comes in so many different shades 自报研究主题，开头的研究自述句就是全篇主旨落点，后文各段都在回答这两个 why。 

 【替换】 why skin comes in so many different shades around the world ↔ The color of human skin. different shades=color of skin 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 文中确实多次把 hair 与 skin 对照，听到就想选 The relation between hair and skin.，但毛发只是解释肤色变深的铺垫，不是全篇主题，属以偏概全。  借用原文：we mostly lost their coat of fur 

 B) 未提及 The growing interest in skin studies. 说皮肤研究兴趣日增，原文只说讲者自己在研究皮肤，从未提整个领域兴趣上升，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 文中提过深色皮肤可当天然防晒（a natural sun protector），听到 protector 易选 The need of skin protection.，但防护只是肤色变深的一个功能，不是全篇主旨，属以偏概全。  借用原文：to serve as a natural sun protector

questions.prompt: What had probably caused humans to lose most of their hair one and a half million years ago?
options: The necessity to save energy.
Adaptation to the hot environment.
The need to breathe with ease.
Dramatic climate changes on earth.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What had probably caused humans to lose most of their hair one and a half million years ago? 

 【翻译】 一百五十万年前可能是什么导致人类失去了大部分毛发? 
 A)  节省能量的必要性。 
 B)  对炎热环境的适应。 
 C)  轻松呼吸的需要。 
 D)  地球上剧烈的气候变化。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Adaptation to the hot environment. 
 【定位】 P3 We think we lost this hair because of the need to keep ourselves cool when we were moving around vigorously in a hot environment. 
 我们认为之所以失去毛发，是因为在炎热环境中剧烈活动时需要让身体保持凉爽。 

 【信号】 因果词because引出原因 。because of the need to keep ourselves cool when we were moving around vigorously in a hot environment 里的 because of 是明确的因果信号，它后面这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 the need to keep ourselves cool when we were moving around vigorously in a hot environment ↔ Adaptation to the hot environment. 保持凉爽=适应炎热环境 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The necessity to save energy. 说为节省能量，原文讲的是为散热降温（keep cool），从未提省能量，属未提及。 
 C) 与原文相反 原文提到 We can't really lose heat by breathing quickly，听到 breathe 易选 The need to breathe with ease.，但原文是说人不能靠喘气散热，故才出汗失毛发，与轻松呼吸正相反。  借用原文：We can't really lose heat by breathing quickly and loudly like dogs 

 D) 未提及 Dramatic climate changes on earth. 说地球气候剧变，原文只说在炎热环境中活动需降温，没说气候发生剧烈变化，属未提及兼过度推断。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say protected early humans from the sun?
options: Leaves and grass.
Man-made shelter.
Their skin coloring.
Hair on their skin.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say protected early humans from the sun? 

 【翻译】 说话者说什么保护了早期人类免受阳光伤害? 
 A)  树叶和草。 
 B)  人造庇护所。 
 C)  他们的皮肤颜色。

 【答案】 C （细节题） Their skin coloring.

 基本上，我们让皮肤变深，以作为天然的防晒物，取代我们失去的毛发。 

 【信号】 serve as点明承担保护功能 。we turned our skin darker to serve as a natural sun protector in the place of the hair we lost 里 serve as a natural sun protector 直接点明承担防晒功能的是变深的皮肤，in the place of the hair 又排除了毛发。 

 【替换】 we turned our skin darker to serve as a natural sun protector ↔ Their skin coloring. 变深的皮肤=肤色 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Leaves and grass. 树叶草丛，原文从未提早期人类用植物遮阳，属未提及。 
 B) 未提及 Man-made shelter. 人造遮蔽物，原文讲的是早期人类靠身体本身（皮肤）防晒，没提人造设施，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What happened after humans migrated from Africa to other parts of the world?
options: Their genetic makeup began to change.
Their communities began to grow steadily.
Their children began to mix with each other.
Their pace of evolution began to quicken.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What happened after humans migrated from Africa to other parts of the world? 

 【翻译】 人类从非洲迁徙到世界其他地区后发生了什么? 
 A)  他们的基因构成开始改变。 
 B)  他们的群落开始稳步增长。 
 C)  他们的孩子开始相互混合。 
 D)  他们的进化速度开始加快。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Their genetic makeup began to change. 
 【定位】 P7 These early ancestors of modern Eurasians dispersed into parts of the world that had more seasonal sunshine and much lower levels of sun radiation. It's in these populations that we begin to see real changes in the genetic makeup of natural coloring. 
 这些现代欧亚人的早期祖先扩散到了阳光更具季节性、太阳辐射水平低得多的地区。正是在这些人群中，我们开始看到天然肤色的基因构成发生了真正的变化。 

 【信号】 扩散之后begin to see变化 。原文先讲祖先 dispersed into 别处，紧接着用 we begin to see real changes in the genetic makeup of natural coloring 给出迁徙之后的结果，begin to see 后那句即答案。 

 【替换】 we begin to see real changes in the genetic makeup of natural coloring ↔ Their genetic makeup began to change. changes in genetic makeup=genetic makeup began to change 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Their communities began to grow steadily. 说社群稳步壮大，原文讲的是迁徙后基因变化，从未提社群规模增长，属未提及。 
 C) 张冠李戴 原文末段确有 having children with new mixtures of skin color genes，听到 mix/children 易选 Their children began to mix with each other.，但那是讲今天大城市的混居，不是迁出非洲之后那个时点，时间张冠李戴。  借用原文：new mixtures of people coming together and having children 

 D) 过度推断 Their pace of evolution began to quicken. 说进化加速，原文只说看到基因构成变化，从未说进化速度变快，属过度推断。
